_about: Lane B6: test bench mode's physics figures (scripts/mech/bench_rig.gd reads this; "entries" lists the mech designs the bench can load, one entry per mech id in mechs.json; the per-actuator figures live in parts.json under each actuator's "bench"). Every number here is a reasoned draft, not a measurement of real hardware: change it here, never in code. Units are in the key names.

motor._about: How an actuator's parts.json figures turn into limits. rated_* is what parts.json calls rated (the continuous design point). The torque-speed line runs from stall torque (rated x peak_torque_factor, at zero speed) to zero torque at the no-load speed, passing through (rated torque, rated speed). Electrical input power is the mechanical power plus copper heat; copper heat is heat_w x (torque / rated torque)^2 (current follows torque), so holding a load without moving still costs heat. A part without rotary figures (the older linear templates) is turned into torque with its lever arm.

thermal._about: Winding temperature: heat in = copper heat; heat out = cooling_w_per_k x (temperature - ambient). parts.json may give cooling_w_per_k; otherwise it is cooling_share x the rated heat spread over the climb to max_winding_c, so about 70 percent of rated torque is the most an actuator can hold for ever. From derate_from_c the available torque falls linearly to derate_floor of full at max_winding_c, where the thermal cutout trips (a drive that has folded back and still cannot shed the heat); it resets once the winding is reset_below_derate_c under the derate point. Rotary figures without their own temperatures use the values here.

failure._about: A joint asked for more than shock_fail_factor x its peak torque breaks (a sheared screw or stripped gear train) once the overload has built up to shock_fail_s: each tick over counts its length times how far over the limit it is (capped at 50x), so one tick of a huge impact is as bad as a longer moderate overload. It stays broken until the bench is reset and the leg then holds nothing. What the ground asks of a leg is the spring force, or, once the leg has closed up past travel_frac of its rest length against its end stop, the force of stopping its share of the body over stop_m: a hard landing. Toggled by Settings > Gameplay > Physics > Failures (off: limits still apply, nothing latches).

supply._about: The battery and its bus (drive_efficiency: share of the bus power left after holding the body up that becomes push along the ground; jump_efficiency: kinetic energy over this is what a jump costs the pack). nominal_v matches the voltage the parts.json figures imply (power_w / current_a). Terminal voltage sags with current through internal_mohm; the motors' no-load speed follows the voltage (back-EMF), so a sagging bus slows every joint. max_discharge_kw is the pack's limit; asking for more browns the bus out and every joint's power is cut to what the pack gives. Open-circuit voltage falls from nominal to empty_v_frac of it as the charge drops. No regeneration (a joint being driven by the load wastes the energy as heat), regen_share can turn some back on.

gait._about: How the joint limits bend walking: step_speed_share is the share of the hip's no-load speed the swinging foot may use; sag_floor stops a flat battery or a hot joint stopping the mech dead (the legs can still creep).

grounds._about: The two bench grounds (maps.json test_bench_flat / test_bench_rough read their block here). flat: a level concrete pad with painted marks every 10 m and two ramps. rough: noise-height rock field, amplitude_m high at wavelength_m, plus steps and a boulder strip.

readout._about: The bench HUD (scripts/ui/bench_hud.gd): bar colours turn to warning at warn_frac of the limit and to alarm at alarm_frac; temperature warns at the derate point and alarms 10 degrees below the trip.
